title: Common envelope
description: The provenance every record carries. Kind schemas in v1/ reference these property definitions one by one, because the validator's keyword subset has no allOf.

id.description: Slug; immutable once merged; equals the file name.

aliases.description: Former ids only. Unique across all ids and all other aliases.

authors.description: Contributors to this record, set from the issue opener by the Action. Never free text alone.

license.description: Validated per directory (rule 12). CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 exists for imported geometry, which data/LICENSE does not cover; it is allowed under data/presences/ and, for the actors an import creates, under data/actors/.

review.description: What a reviewer should look at before signing this record, and why. Optional, and written by whoever drafted it; the review dashboard shows it as a filter and Sign removes it. Never a claim about the world — only about how much the record has been checked.

citations.description: Which of this record's citations a person has opened and checked against the source itself, keyed by the cited source's id (rule 3 checks the key is a source the record cites). A citation with no entry here has not been checked; the validator counts those and Sign warns about them without blocking. Never a claim about the world — only about how far this record has been read.

verified.description: Who checked this citation and on what day; null is a citation somebody looked at and did not confirm, which is not the same as one nobody has opened.

wikidata.description: The Wikidata item this record is about: Q followed by digits. Optional and additive — written by the import, or derived by the contribution form from a pasted Wikidata URL — and unique among records of the same kind (rule 21). It is an identifier and never a source: what the atlas asserts is in the record.

wikipedia.description: Language code to article title: { "en": "Carnation Revolution" }. Allowed only beside a wikidata id (rule 21), because a title with no item behind it is a guess about which article is meant. Written by the import.

sitelinks.description: How many language editions have an article for the item. A stored fact for an editorial decision nobody has taken: it feeds neither prominence nor weight, and the map's measure stays the derived weight (ARCHITECTURE.md).

sources.description: Citations. A citation points at a source record by id, with an optional locator (page, chapter, folio).
